selections.reason: The replay targets the dominant flow error, while the separate price output preserves a channel for own-trade impact.
Separate replay should reduce induced background bias, while the own-trade output can preserve direct price impact.
Baseline already strong; separating background replay risks perturbing calibrated bias with no clear RMSE/NLL gain, and mixed joint+own-trade changes add parameters without evidence of net benefit.
Separate no-injection background replay should reduce background bias and the own-trade indicator/output should improve execution-response fit with modest effect on full metrics.
The error decomposition favors testing an own-trade price head while holding the background model fixed.
C3 tests whether an own-trade price output improves fit without also changing the background model.
Own-trade features likely aid fit while retaining validated background weights, minimizing disruption risk.
Own-trade indicator plus separate own-trade output should reduce execution error while preserving baseline background, limiting risk versus C2.
Separate-trade background replay keeps baseline price weights, preserving fit while reducing bias without extra own-trade modeling risks.
